title: The First Traffic Light Exploded
source: Science Museum — Romans to raves: A history of roads and motorways
narration: The world's first traffic light was built before cars even existed. In 1868, horse-drawn carriages jammed the streets outside Britain's Houses of Parliament, so railway engineer John Peake Knight adapted a semaphore signal for the road. Two mechanical arms told drivers to stop or move with caution. After dark, a gas lamp rotated red and green lenses into view. Nothing was automatic. A police officer stood beside the machine and worked its lever by hand. But beneath the lamp, gas began leaking. Less than a month after installation, the signal exploded and injured the officer operating it. London abandoned the experiment. Decades later, electric signals returned—and today's traffic lights grew from a Victorian machine that failed spectacularly.
